back: A computerised till that captures product and payment data and updates stock records.
Barcode read → code found in stock file → price and description returned → stock level reduced → compared with reorder level.
Card read → PIN checked → amount chosen → balance checked → cash dispensed → account updated.
Optical mark recognition: detects marks in set positions on a form (answer sheets, registers).
Optical character recognition: converts scanned text images into editable characters.
Magnetic ink character recognition: reads magnetic-ink numbers on cheques; accurate and hard to forge.
Radio frequency identification: tags with a chip and antenna are read by radio, without line of sight.
Chip: encrypted data, hard to clone, used with a PIN. Stripe: cheap but easily skimmed.

front: Why barcodes do not store prices
back: Only the product code is stored; prices are looked up in the database so they can change without reprinting.
